## APPENDIX P

### BYLAWS

OF

### PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH IN AMERICA (A CORPORATION)

As Amended by the Ninth General Assembly

### ARTICLE I. NAME AND LOCATION.

Sectlon 1. The name of this corporation shall be Presbyterian Church in America (A  
Corporation).  
Sectlon 2. The registered office in the State of Delaware is to be located at 229  
South State Street, in the City of Dover, County of Kent. The registered agent in charge  
thereof is The Prentice-Hall Corporation System, Inc. at 229 South State Street, Dover,  
Delaware. The official business address of the Corporation is the office of the Business  
Administrator.  
Other offices for transaction of business shall be located at such places as the  
General Assembly or its Permanent Committees shall designate.

### ARTICLE II. MEMBERS AND MEETINGS OF THE CORPORATION

Sectlon 1. The members of the corporation shall be those duly ordained Teaching Elders (Ministers) enrolled in a Presbytery affillated with the Presbyterian Church in America, and those Ruling Elders representing local congregations, which congregations are affillated with Presbyterles affiliated with the Presbyterian Church in America who have designated or commissioned to attend the annual General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church in America. Such Teaching EIders and Ruling EIders shall be designated or commissioned by Presbyteries or Congregations in accordance with rules and regulations prescribed by the Book of Church Order(14-2)(See Article VI). Such Individuals shall be the members of the corporation until the next annual meeting of the General Assembly of the Presbyterlan Church in America at which time the members of the Corporation shall be those individuals designated or commissioned as hereinabove set forth to attend such annual General Assembly. Sectlon 2. The annual meeting of the Corporation shall be at such time and such place as designated by the General Assembly. Each General Assembly shall have the power to deslgnate the time and place for more than one annual General Assembly, and shall also have the power to authorize the Committee on Administration to designate the time and place of the next General Assembly. Sectlon 3. Speclal meetings of the General Assembly may be called in accordance with the Book of Church Order (14-3). Sectlon 4. A quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the General Assembly shall be that prescribed in the Book of Church Order (14-5). Sectlon 5. The Moderator shall call all meetings to order and shall preside until his successor has been selected and takes office. If the Moderator is unable to act, the Stated Clerk shall call the Assembly to order and preside over its sessions until a Moderator has been elected. Sectlon 6. Proxies shall not be allowed at General Assembly meetings.

### ARTICLE I11. OFFICERS.

Sectlon 1. The officers of the Corporation shall be the Moderator, the Clerk, the Business Administrator-treasurer, and such assistant clerks and treasurers as may be deemed desirable by the Committee on Administration. The officers, with exception of the assistant clerks or assistant treasurers, shall be elected by the General Assembly as set forth in the Book of Church Order and the Rules for Assembly Operation. In the event that the Stated Clerk or the Business Administrator is unable to act, the Committee on Administration shall be authorized to appoint a provislonal Clerk or a provisional Business Administrator to serve until a regular Clerk or Business Administrator may be elected by the next General Assembly. Sectlon 2. The Moderator shall have such duties and responsibilities as set forth In the Book of Church Order and the Rules of Assembly Operation. The Moderator, unless specifically authorized by the General Assembly, shall have no authority to and shall not be expected to perform any functions for the Corporation other than those specifically set forth in these Bylaws or those set forth In the Book of Church Order, and the Rules for Assembly Operation. Sectlon 3. The Clerk shall have such duties and responsibilities as set forth in the Book of Church Order and Rules of Assembly Operation. He shall be Immediately responsible to the Committee on Administration. The Clerk shall prepare and forward all notices requlred by law or by these Bylaws, and shall have general charge of the corporate books and records. He shall sign such instruments as may be required, and perform the duties Incident to the office of Clerk, and such duties as may be assigned by the Moderator, the Committee on Administration, or the members of the Corporation in General Assembly.

<a id="ga09-p377"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=9 pdf_page=377 printed_page=null -->

Sectlon 4. The Business Administrator-treasurer shall be the custodian of the funds and securities belonging to the Corporation, and not otherwise designated to one of the three program Committees. He shall receive deposlt and disburse such funds as directed by the General Assembly, including any provislons set forth in the Book of Church Order. He shall keep an accurate account of the finances of the Corporation, not only of these funds in the custody, but by means of monthly reports from the other Committees of their funds also, on a uniform form, which he shall provide. He shall prepare or have prepared such reports of the financial condition of the Corporation as be required, and, in general, perform all of the dutles Incident to the office of Business Administrator-treasurer. He shall be bonded in an amount to be determined by the Committee on Administration.

### ARTICLE IV. PERMANENT COMMITTEES.

Sectlon 1. The affairs of the Corporatlon shall be conducted primarily through Permanent Committees, to wit: Committee on Administration; Committee for ChrIstian Education and Publlcatlons; CommIttee on Mission to the United States; and Committee on Mission to the World. Each committee shall be composed of slx Teaching Elders and six Rullng EIders divided Into four classes of three men each serving four-year terms. There shall also be a Permanent Sub-Committee on Judiclal Business composed of elght members divided Into four classes of two members each serving four-year terms. Each class shall be composed of one TeachIng Elder and one Ruling EIder. The Moderator, the Immediate past Moderator, the Stated Clerk and one representative each of the Committee for ChrIstian Education and Publicatlons, the Committee on Mission to the United States, the Committee on Mission to the World, and the Sub-Committee on Judiclal Buslness shall be advisory members of the Committee on Adminlstration. An advisory member shall be able to participate freely In the conduct of the business of the Committee, but he shall have no vote. Sectlon 2. The Power and authorlty of the Permanent Committees shall be those set forth In these Bylaws or by directlon of the General Assembly. Section 3. The Permanent Committees shall, unless specifically directed otherwise by the General Assembly, be authorized to operate from separate locations with separate offices and separate staffs. The budget for each Permanent Committee, including specifically the compensatlon to be pald the chlef administrative officer of each Permanent Committee, shall be submitted to the Committee on Stewardship Ministrles, which shall consider the requests of each.Committee as it relates to the budget requests of other Committees, to needs, and to opportunltles, and shall recommend an overall budget to the General Assembly, for its approval. All funds recelved by the Corporation that are designated for the benefit of any particular Permanent Committee shall be disbursed by the Business Administrator to the proper Committee. There shall be no equallzation of funds so designated. Any funds recelved by the Corporation not designated as belng for the benef It of a particular Permanent Committee shall be distributed by the Business Adminlstrator as directed by the General Assembly. Sectlon 4. Each Permanent Committee, by resolution adopted by a majority of Its Committee members, may deslgnate the place, date, and time for regular meetings of the Committee, which should be held at least quarterly. Written or printed notice of such resolution should be glven to all Committee members within a reasonable time af ter the adoption thereof. Notice of the time, place or purpose of such regular meetings of the Permanent Committee shall not be required to be given. Section 5. Speclal meetings of the Permanent Committees may be called at any time or place by the Chalrman of the Committee, or by a majorlty of the Committee members. Written notice stating the place, date, and hour of such speclal meeting shall be dellvered by the Chalrman of the Committee to each Committee member at least ten days prlor to the date of such meetings, and such notice should specify the purpose of such speclal meetings. Attendance of a Committee member at such a meeting will constitute a walver of notice of such meeting. The act of the majority of the Committee members present at a meeting at which a quorum is present shall be the act of the Committee. Sectlon 6. A majority of a Permanent Committee shall constitute a quorum. Sectlon 7. The Chalrman and the Secretary of each Permanent Committee shall be elected annually at the first meeting of the Committee following the General Assembly. The electlon of the Chairman and Secretary shall not take place untll after 10 days notice of the proposed meeting has been given to all newly nominated members and all continuing members. The incumbent Chalrman and Secretary shall continue to serve untll their successors have been elected and assume their dutles. In the event that the Chalrman is rotated off of a Committee, the Moderator of the General Assembly shall name a Convener of the Committee, who shall preslde over the Committee untll a Chairman Is elected and assume his duties. Sectlon 8. In the event any administrative personnel employed by a Committee and approved by the General Assembly is unable to act, such Committee may employ a provlslonal replacement, who has been examined and approved by the Assembly's Theological Examining Committee, and who shall serve untll the next General Assembly. Section 9. The Individual Permanent Committees

<a id="ga09-p378"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=9 pdf_page=378 printed_page=null -->

- **A.** The Committee on Administration.

1. The business affalrs of the Corporation as distingulshed from the eccleslastical matters, and those not speclfically assigned to one of the other Permanent Committees by these Bylaws or an act of the General Assembly, shall be managed by the Committee on Administratlon, which serves as the Board of Directors provided in the Charter of Incorporation, subject to such rules and regulations as may be prescribed by the General Assembly, Including all applicable provislons of the Book of Church Order.

2. The Committee on Administration shall hold an annual meeting in conjunction with the annual General Assembly meeting, at a time and place to be determined by the Committee. Notice shall not be required to be given of the time or place of the annual meeting of the Committee, other than that which shall be Included in the Commissloner's Handbook for the General Assembly.

- **B.** The Committee for Christian Education and Publlcatlons. The affalrs of the Church In the areas of Christian education and publicatlons are assigned to the Committee for Christlan Education and Publlcatlons, whose duties and authority shall be deslgnated by the General Assembly.

- **C.** The CommIttee on Mission to the United States. The affairs of the Church Involved In Its extenslon In the Unlted States and Canada are asslgned to the Committee on Mission to the Unlted States, whose dutles and author- Ity shall be designated by the General Assembly.

- **D.** The Committee on Mission to the World. The affalrs of the Church in the area of world missions outside of the United States and Canada are asslgned to the Committee on Mission to the World, whose duties and authority shall be designated by the General Assembly.

- **E.** The Sub-committee on Judiclal Business. The Sub-committee on Judicial Business shall advise the Assembly on all constitutlonal matters, and between Assemblles shall function as advisory to the Stated Clerk and the Committee on AdmInistratlon. The Sub-committee shall not be separately funded but administratively will operate as a Sub-committee of the Committee on Adminlstration. The Sub-committee will make direct report to each Assembly.

- **F.** Other Committees The Assembly may elect or appolnt other committees of elther a permanent or temporary character to handle particular matters of business as designated by the Assembly. The business handled by such committees shall be limited to those matters assigned by the Assembly. The membershlp of other permanent committees, sub-committees, boards or agencles shall be limited to the same constitutional provislons (BC) 14-1-12) as those of the permanent committees: to wit, that those who have served for at least a full term, or at least two years of a partlal term on one of the Assembly's permanent committees, or permanent sub-committees, or other agencles shall not be ellglble for reelectlon to an Assembly committee or agency until one year has elapsed. Nominatlons shall be handled according to the BC014-2-11. No IndlvIdual shall serve on more than one Assembly committee, sub-committee, board or agency at one time. Employees of the Assembly's committees, or agencles are not ellgible for office on an Assembly's committee, sub-committee, board or agency, which administers matters directly related to their area of employment.

- **G.** Boards When It is necessary for the handllng of civil matters for the Assembly to authorize one of Its committees, sub-committees, or agencles to Incorporate and to form a board, the relationship of the board to the Assembly remalns as a committee or subcommittee, and the provislons of the corporation charter and bylaws shall be In conformity with the constitution of the Church. The rules for membership and electlon of these boards shall be the same as provlded for in the BCo 14-1, except that the number of classes and lengths of terms may vary.

- **H.** Exceptlons The Assembly has auuthority to make exceptions to the above guldellnes for those sub-committees or agencies not specifically covered by the Boo, by making amendments to these bylaws spelllng out the specific exceptions, as well as approving corporation bylaws In conformity with these exceptions. Sectlon 10. The Sub-committee on Stewardship Ministrles. This Committee shall operate adminlstratively as a Sub-Committee of the Committee on Administration. The Committee will make direct report to each Assembly. This Sub- Committee shall be consldered as a Permanent Sub-Committee as to continulty; but it shall not be considered as a Permanent Sub-Committee under Book of Church Order, Sectlon 15-1(12), as it relates to nominations and servlce. This Committee shall

<a id="ga09-p379"></a>
<!-- PAGE ga=9 pdf_page=379 printed_page=null -->

consist of one Ruling Elder and one Teaching Elder from the active or alternate members of each of the following four Permanent Committees, to wit: Mission to the World, Mission to the United States, Administration, and Christian Educatlon and Publlcations. These Committee members shall be assigned by each of four Permanent Committees, above named, and shall serve at the pleasure of such Permanent Committee. The Coordinators of sald four Permanant Committees and the Director of Stewardshlp Ministrles, the Managing Director of the PCA Foundation, the Moderator and the Stated Clerk of the General Assembly shall be advlsory members of this Committee. Sectlon 11. Board of Trustees of the Insurance and Annuity Fund. The Board of Trustees of the Insurance and Annulty Funds of the Presbyterlan Church In America, herelnafter referred to as "Trustees", shall exerclse such powers and conduct such business as delegated to It by the General Assembly from time to time. SpeclfIcally, but not in limitation thereof, the Trustees shall adminlster the Annulty plans, the group Insurance programs and the rellef programs of the Corporation. No action of the General Assembly or the Corporation shall conf lict with provisions of the "Trust Agreement for the Annulty Funds for ministers of the Presbyterlan Church In America," and the "Trust Agreement for the Annulty Fund for Lay Employees of the Presbyterlan Church In AmerIca" without amendment of sald Trust Agreements as provided In the Trust Agreements. The Trustees will make a report to each General Assembly through the Committee of Commlssloners on Insurance. The Trustees shall not be subject to the control or direction of any other Committee or organlzatlon of the Corporation. The Trustees shall be ten (10) in number, divided Into five (5) classes of two (2) meneach servlng five (5) year terms. The General Assembly shall elect at each Assembly a class of Trustees to begin service Immedlately following the concluslon of the Assembly. Each member of the Trustees must be elther a Teaching Elder, Ruling Elder or Deacon In the Presbyterlan Church In AmerIca. The Trustees are not subject to the provislons of the BC0. Chapter 15 relating to proportionate representation of all Presbyterles or for equal representation of Teachlng and Ruling Elders.

### ARTICLE V. FISCAL MATTERS.

Sectlon 1. The fiscal year of the Corporation shall be from January 1 through December 31 of each year. The General Assembly shall annually deslgnate the auditors of the Corporation on recommendation from the Committee on Adminlstration, which auditing firm shall make an audif of the financlal affairs of the Corporation and of each Permanent Committee promptly following the close of each fiscal year. The expenses of such audit shall be prorated among the Corporation and each Permanent Committee. Sectlon 2. All funds of the Corporation shall be deposlted from time to time to the credit of the Corporation In such banks, savings and loan Institutlons, trust, or other depositorles as the Permanent Committees by resolutlon may select. Soction 3. All checks, drafts, or other orders for the payment of money, notes, or other evidences of debtedness Issued in the name of the Corporation shall be signed by such officer or officers of the Corporation as the Committee on Adminlstration shall deslgnate. All checks, drafts, or other orders for the payment of money, notes, or other evldences of Indebtedness Issued in the name of any of the Permanent Committees shall be signed by such representative of the Committee as the Committee by resolution shall deslgnate.

### ARTICLE VI. ECCLESIASTICAL MATTERS.

Sectlon 1. The eccleslastical Constitution of the Church is composed of: the Westminster Confesslon of Falth, the Larger and Shorter CatechIsms as adopted by the General Assembly of the Presbyterlan Church In AmerIca, and the Book of Church Order of the Presbyterlan Church In AmerIca. The provislons of the Constitutlon shall control over any provisions of these Bylaws that may be In conf lict therewith.

### ARTICLE VII. AMENDMENTS TO THE BYLAWS

These Bylaws may be amended by a majority vote at any annual or speclal meeting of the General Assembly.
